videos.title: Balatro Basics: Skip Tag Tier List (You're doing it wrong)
videos.why: Prices every skip tag against the hidden cost of a skip (your best future round plus a lost shop); verdict: almost never skip, with ante 1 Small Blind (and start of ante 2) exceptions. Version 1.0.0n.

videos.title: Updated Skip Tag Tier List (Balatro 101 Patch)
videos.why: 1.0.1 changes: Investment pays $25 (up a rank), joker tags make the joker free (same skip situations), Top-up up and Negative down at sticker stakes. Current view.

videos.title: Balatro Basics: All Consumables Tier List
videos.why: Live-stream tier list of every Tarot, Planet and Spectral for an 8-ante run, including his poker-hand ranking for Planets (Straight best). Version 1.0.1c.

claims.statement: A skip does not cost the current round's reward: the run has a fixed number of rounds, so a skip removes your last and best future round and shop (the one with most interest, value jokers, gold cards and purple seals). A tag is worth a skip only if it beats that best future round, which at White stake is large.

conditions.stake: any (he says the White-stake ceiling is high, so the cost is larger there)

quotes.text: is the skip worth not just what I'm skipping now but is it worth my theoretical best round in the future
I don't get to see that shop because I've skipped not just the current round but the future whatever my best future round is

claims.knob: value of a skip = tag value - value of a late-game round (cash + interest + joker/seal income + one shop); skip only when > 0
claims.notes: Roffle states it only for Gold; BU applies it to all stakes.

claims.statement: Benchmark: nearly every tag is worth a skip only in ante 1, usually only on the Small Blind (Big Blind skip 'maybe'); from ante 2 on, don't skip for them. His closing verdict: never skip, except maybe.

quotes.text: you only take these in anti1 you probably only take these if they're the small blind skip big blind skip maybe
that's how bad all of these tags are is you only take it in anti1
this is how I feel about Skip tags never skip except maybe

claims.knob: allow skip only when ante == 1 and blind == Small (Big only for the strongest tags); never skip ante >= 2 except the specific ante-2 tags (Top-up/Buffoon) and Orbital-on-main-hand
claims.notes: Exceptions he gives elsewhere: Top-up/Buffoon at the start of ante 2, Orbital when it hits your hand, Handy/Economy maybe later.

claims.statement: A skip makes you face higher blinds with the same jokers; he frames each skipped round as roughly a +50% score requirement the tag would have to cover. With weak scoring (his Gold-stake runs with -1 hand / -1 discard) skipping the Small Blind with no scoring joker loses the Big Blind about 40% of the time. Skip only when the current build already beats the next blind with margin.

conditions.stake: mainly high stakes (Gold as of 1.0.0: -1 hand size, -1 discard)

quotes.text: if I take a skip is the skip whatever the reward is is it worth a 50% increase in score
I would say maybe 40% of the time 40% of the time you can't beat the big blind
skipping too much or skipping at all often is going to end you if you're not able to keep up with the scoring requirements

claims.knob: skip only if projected best-hand score of current build >= 1.5 x next blind requirement (and boss after it is beatable)
claims.notes: The 40% figure is for the old 1.0.0 Gold stake (-1 hand size). In zWNty-x3g_M he notes 1.0.1 Gold no longer has -1 hand size. The '50%' is his rough framing, not an exact blind ratio.

claims.statement: Every shop has value: two free joker offers plus fresh booster packs. In ante 1 there are two shops before the boss (four joker chances); one skip halves that to two. Many ante 1-2 losses come from seeing too few shops.

quotes.text: normally you get two shops two shops between you and the boss that gives you four cards four chances to pick up the scoring help that you need
maybe you didn't see enough shops is what the issue is

claims.knob: skip penalty term includes one lost shop (2 joker offers + 2 packs) valued at roughly a reroll-plus-packs; heavier when joker count < 2

claims.statement: Jokers are by far the most efficient way to raise score; going from 2 to 3 jokers is huge and 4 to 5 is still big. Planets/Tarots help but are much less efficient.

quotes.text: the most efficient way to improve your score in the game is with Jokers obviously
two and three Jokers is huge the difference between four and five Jokers is still pretty big

claims.knob: shop priority: fill joker slots (scoring) before consumables; marginal value of joker #3 > joker #5 but both high

claims.statement: Once you are at the $25 interest cap, buy as many booster packs as you can (Arcana and Celestial always; Standard optional). Buying a Celestial or Arcana pack is more efficient than rerolling the shop hoping for Planets or Tarots.

quotes.text: when you have $25 or more you know when you have your interest cap then buy as many booster packs as you can
it is more efficient to buy a Celestial pack than it is to roll the show roll the shop hoping to find some Planet cards

roffle.note: BU: at the cap, buy every Arcana/Celestial pack (he admits in zWNty-x3g_M this sometimes costs interest); Roffle: from ante 3 leave every shop with >= $25.

claims.knob: if money >= 25: buy every Arcana/Celestial (and Spectral) pack in the shop; prefer packs over rerolls when the target is a Planet/Tarot
claims.notes: Wording is ambiguous on whether he would go below $25 to do it; in zWNty-x3g_M (Hermit) he says you can't afford every pack and lose interest when you try, so the conflict is soft.

claims.statement: Standard packs are the optional pack: buy them only when you have spare money and the deck can take cards (purple/red seals, gold cards); when you need to save for rerolls for scoring jokers, skip them. Never skip a blind for a Standard pack.

quotes.text: what I need to do is save my money for rerolling for better Jokers scoring jokers in which case Okay sometimes I don't want a standard pack
I always want Celestial I always want Arcana I sometimes don't want standard packs
never worth it to skip for a standard pack get out of here

claims.knob: Standard pack buy only if money - price >= reserve for rerolls (e.g. >= 25 + 5) and scoring jokers are sufficient; Standard Tag skip = never

claims.statement: Garbage Tag is useless over 90% of the time (you should be using discards to find hands, gold cards and purple seals); Speed Tag ($5 per skip) is a joke because you should not be skipping. Bottom tier.

quotes.text: more than 90% of the time this is going to be a blank this is going to be useless to you
the speed tag here is kind of a joke gives you $5

claims.knob: tag value Garbage ~ $0-5, Speed = $5 x skips; never skip for either

claims.statement: Holographic Tag is an all-star only on the ante 1 round 1 (Small Blind) skip: a guaranteed +10 Mult joker in the first shop carries you through ante 2 (first six rounds), so you can bank interest or buy value jokers. Worth at least two rerolls ($10-12). At Gold stake always take it (and Foil) in round 1; at White it is not needed but reasonable if you struggle with early scoring. Foil (+50 chips) is slightly worse than Holographic. Once you have any scoring joker, don't skip for it.

quotes.text: if I get a holographic in round one that is enough scoring to carry me through all of anti2
I think this skip here is worth at least you know $10 or $12
if we're talking about gold Stakes then you always take them in round one if we're talking about white staks I don't think you need it

roffle.note: BU: at Gold always skip round 1 for Holographic/Foil; Roffle: at Gold play every small and big blind.

claims.knob: ante 1 Small Blind: skip if tag in {Holographic, Foil} and joker_count == 0 (Gold always; White: test both); tag value Holo ~ $12, Foil ~ $10
claims.notes: 1.0.1 (Lx2bAMdKwIs): the edition joker is now also free, so these skips are 'more worth it' in the same situations.

claims.statement: Rule of thumb: 4 Mult ~= 30 chips (Even Steven/Odd Todd, Scary/Smiley Face, Empress/Hierophant), so +10 Mult ~= 75 chips, which is why Foil (+50 chips) is below Holographic. Early on Mult matters most (a +4 Mult Jimbo doubles an 80 x 4 hand), but there are more Mult jokers than chips jokers, so the first chips source gets more valuable as Mult stacks; long term you want Mult because chips come from other sources (Planets).

quotes.text: the conversion rate is four mol is the same as 30 chips
it is easier to find more Mt you can have three or four Mt Jokers finding that first chips Joker could be challenging
I think long term longterm you're going to want to have the Mt because you can get chips from other sources

claims.knob: joker scorer baseline: 1 Mult = 7.5 chips; weight +Mult x1.2 early (ante 1-2); add a bonus to the first +Chips joker when owned +Mult jokers >= 3 and +Chips jokers == 0
claims.notes: zWNty-x3g_M adds the planet-side corollary: chips per level matter most because Mult comes from jokers.

claims.statement: Don't take the Polychrome Tag in ante 1: after skipping you cannot afford the joker (edition raises price; from Red stake no Small Blind reward), and early x1.5 is far weaker than +10 Mult (on a 75 x 4 hand +10 Mult is +250%, x1.5 is +50%). Later you find better xMult anyway and end up selling it.

quotes.text: if you're in anti-1 you can't take this the reason why you can't take this is because you can't afford it
the holographic is way bigger early and then later on in the game you can easily find other sources of xol

claims.knob: Polychrome Tag: never skip in ante 1 (1.0.0 pricing); in 1.0.1 joker is free, still rank below Holographic early
claims.notes: Affordability argument is from 1.0.0; 1.0.1 made tag jokers free (Lx2bAMdKwIs) but he says skip situations do not expand.

claims.statement: Investment Tag: in 1.0.0 ($15 after the boss) not worth a skip and never from ante 2 on, since you skip a shop and have nothing to spend it on. In 1.0.1 it pays $25, a big upgrade that moves it up one rank, still an ante 1 consideration.

quotes.text: if you see this anti-2 or later you don't want this
previously giving us $15 after the boss now gives us $25 is a huge upgrade
I feel you know fine moving it up a rank

claims.knob: tag value Investment = $25 paid after the boss (1.0.1); consider only ante 1 Small Blind; never ante >= 2
claims.notes: Updated video (1.0.1) supersedes the $15 valuation.

claims.statement: Economy Tag has the highest raw value of any tag (doubles money, max +$40) but he usually still doesn't take it: even at $40 a round can earn more than $40 of value, and at high stakes the higher requirements after a skip end the run. Its value peaks once you can hold about $40 (reachable around round 5).

conditions.build_state: money near $40 and build comfortably ahead

quotes.text: even at $40 I can make more than $40 worth of value in a round
maybe there is some ante where I would take it but most of the time I don't take it
I think economy tag just uh the raw value of it is just too powerful

claims.knob: Economy Tag skip only if min(money, 40) >= ~$30 and current build beats next blind with >= 1.5x margin; otherwise play the blind
claims.notes: The '$40 by round five' remark: 'you could get to $40 double your money in round five'.

claims.statement: Coupon Tag is top tier: take it in ante 1 (ante 2 is somewhat reasonable). Free jokers and packs fill your joker slots right away, which lets you win with fewer hands and get the economy going sooner.

quotes.text: this is at least you know um anti1 I think also anti2 is somewhat reasonable
I take the coupon tag I fill up my Joker slots
this is top tier top tier coupon tag maybe not as good as the economy tag

claims.knob: skip for Coupon Tag at ante 1 Small Blind (ante 2 Small if joker_count <= 2); tag value ~ sum of initial shop joker+pack prices

claims.statement: Boss Tag (reroll) and Juggle Tag (+3 hand size for one round) are short-term boss beaters, not worth a shop. Skip for them only when the upcoming boss hard-counters your build (e.g. debuffs your flush suit or your face cards); if all bosses are weak or all strong, a reroll does nothing. Boss reroll > Juggle. 1.0.1 adds $5 to these (his hypothetical) would make them 'less bad, not good'.

quotes.text: I think the value of the boss roll depends on how tough the bosses are
if you have you know just a few like hard counters to what you're currently working on then I think
most of the time it's just if the boss is hard give me plus three hand size makes the boss easier

claims.knob: skip for Boss/Juggle Tag only if boss_counter(boss, build) is true (suit debuff on main suit, face debuff on face build, etc.); value otherwise < $15
claims.notes: In Lx2bAMdKwIs the '+$5' is posed as a hypothetical rework, not a stated 1.0.1 change.

claims.statement: Handy Tag pays $1 per hand played; winning in 1-2 hands is about 5 hands per ante, so ~$25 by ante 6 and $35+ by ante 8. Not worth a skip even at $25; if ever, only mid-late (ante 4-5+). He contradicts himself on its rank (first above the ante-1 tags, then 'the worst of all of these').

quotes.text: every antie maybe that's five hands five hands per anti so if you get this in anti six then this is 25 bucks
I think you shouldn't take it I think it's not you know even at 25 bucks is not not worth it
I think the handy tag is the worst of all of these it just gives you the money but it gives you at a time that you don't need it

claims.knob: Handy Tag value = hands_played x $1; skip only if value > late-round value (effectively never before ante 6)
claims.notes: Self-contradiction within q4YAHDuRUcQ about whether Handy ranks above or below the ante-1 joker tags.

claims.statement: Uncommon Tag beats Rare Tag: rares are inflexible build-arounds that often don't fit, while uncommons are flexible (an average uncommon gives about 30-40 Mult vs ~15 for a common), similar to an early Holographic. Skip for Uncommon only in ante 1 (scaling uncommons won't help right away); he would not skip for a Rare even in ante 1.

quotes.text: I think a lot of the time with the rare tag you're going to be disappointed
only an anti1 would I be willing to skip for an uncommon
15 bucks is something that I'd be willing to take in anti1 whereas the rare skip I wouldn't be willing to take in anti1

claims.knob: Uncommon Tag: skip allowed only ante 1 Small Blind; Rare Tag: never skip
claims.notes: 1.0.1: the tag's joker is now free (Lx2bAMdKwIs) but he keeps the same skip situations.

claims.statement: Negative Tag is worse than a Celestial pack: the random negative is usually a common that doesn't fit, and a free joker slot does not lower the bar, the joker still has to help (in the shop too: don't buy a negative just because it takes no space). In 1.0.1 at higher stakes a third of these are Rentals, so he moves it down further.

quotes.text: I think this is worse than a Celestial pack I think a Celestial pack is better than a random negative
even though it doesn't take up any space that doesn't the bar for it you know helping you is not zero
you have a one and three chance that the negative you get is a rental

claims.knob: Negative Tag: never skip; shop: score a negative joker by its scoring/econ contribution with no bonus for the free slot beyond the slot itself
claims.notes: 1.0.1 Lx2bAMdKwIs: 'I feel even more confident that we can move it down here'.

claims.statement: Pack tags are not worth a skip: Mega Arcana is worth more on average than Mega Celestial (more different cards can help), but neither is worth $15; Spectral (Ethereal) Tag is just 'fine'; Standard Tag never. Individual Planets are worth more than individual Tarots, but an Arcana pack beats a Celestial pack on average.

quotes.text: I think Arcana packs are worth you know more on average than the celestial pack I don't think it's worth as much as $15 though
individual Planet cards are going to be worth more than tarot cards

claims.knob: tag values: Charm (Mega Arcana) < $15, Meteor (Mega Celestial) < Charm, Ethereal < Charm, Standard ~0; pack EV ordering in shop: Arcana > Celestial

claims.statement: Buy a Spectral pack in the first shop or two of the run (Ouija/Sigil to pivot, seals, Grim are strong early). From ante 2 on the cards rarely fit your build and you often take nothing, but it is still worth $4 when you have the money: low cost, small chance of a big hit. Not worth a skip.

quotes.text: in the literal first shop of the game or maybe the first couple shops of the game um I'm going to take a spectr pack
any later on you know in anti2 and further the spectral pack is not going to give you the ones that are actually compatible with what you're doing
I definitely think that the spectral packs are worth the $4 when you buy them however is it worth a Skip and I think not

claims.knob: shop: buy Spectral pack in ante 1 whenever affordable; ante >= 2 buy if money - 4 >= interest floor; allow 'skip all' pick

claims.statement: Game rule he states: in ante 1 the skip tag can't be Top-up, Orbital, Buffoon, Spectral (Ethereal), Negative or Celestial (Meteor); Arcana (Charm) can appear as the first skip (Judgement + Fool can give two jokers).

quotes.text: in round one or in anti1 you can't get the topup tag
you can't get Spectral skip in anti1 either um you can't get a negative skip in anti-1 you can't get a Celestial pack
skip as the first Skip and the Arcana skip can give you judgment cards

claims.knob: simulator/tag model: exclude {Top-up, Orbital, Buffoon, Ethereal, Negative, Meteor} from ante-1 tag pool
claims.notes: Mechanic, verify against game source (tag min_ante).

claims.statement: Top-up Tag (2 commons) and Mega Buffoon Tag are worth it only at the very start of ante 2 (its Small Blind) when joker slots are still open; at high stakes take Top-up then. Buffoon > Top-up (you choose). By ante 3 you likely have 5 jokers, and one reroll shows 4 cards anyway, so almost never later. 1.0.1 at Orange/Gold: Top-up jokers carry no stickers, so it moves above Holographic/Foil.

quotes.text: for you know literally the beginning of anti2 then it's worth it super worth it super powerful just to get the plane off
anti3 you probably have five Jokers already if you already have five Jokers what what are you messing around with buffoon pack
it gives you non stickered Jokers so you can't get perishables you can't get rentals and so I think topup tag for me then moves up a little bit here

claims.knob: ante 2 Small Blind: skip for Buffoon or Top-up Tag if joker_count <= 3 (implied) and build beats Big Blind; ante >= 3 never
claims.notes: 'joker_count <= 3' is implied from 'you're probably going to have the empty Joker slots', not stated.

claims.statement: Orbital Tag (+3 levels to a random hand) is something money can't buy: it matches your hand only ~10% of the time, but then it's worth about $40. Early (ante 2) you can pivot to the upgraded hand, so he takes it about 25% of the time it appears.

conditions.build_state: upgraded hand == main hand, or ante 2 and hand is pivotable

quotes.text: only 10% of the time is this going to be valid but when it is it slaps this is worth 40 bucks
if you get this in anti 2 now you pivot around this
I think a quarter of the time when you see the orbital you take it

claims.knob: skip for Orbital Tag iff tag_hand == main_hand (value ~$40), or ante == 2 and tag_hand in {Straight, Flush, Two Pair, Three of a Kind} with no committed hand yet

claims.statement: Voucher Tag gives something money can't buy (one voucher per ante otherwise); a voucher like +1 hand, +1 discard or Seed Money beats a random negative or rare. He first prices it under $15 (below Investment), then ranks it above Investment, Rare and Polychrome.

quotes.text: money cannot buy you extra vouchers you get one voucher per ante and that's it
I think it's worth probably less than 15 bucks probably less than the investment tag
voucher is better than a rare voucher is more helpful more often than a rare would be

claims.knob: Voucher Tag value ~ $15 (ante 1 only); rank above Investment/Rare/Polychrome tags
claims.notes: Self-contradiction within q4YAHDuRUcQ: first 'less than the investment tag', later 'better than the investment'.

claims.statement: D6 Tag (rerolls start at $0, +$1 each) is underrated: if you'd reroll 3 times anyway it saves $15; late (ante 5-6, when you have reroll money) you can do 7-8 rerolls in one shop; in ante 1, $3 buys three rerolls (six more joker views). Better than Coupon, worse than Economy's $40. Still, you shouldn't skip, but if you skip, consider D6.

quotes.text: that saves you 15 bucks if you reroll if you would have normally been willing to roll three times
I think for me D6 is great D6 is uh way better than you think it is also you shouldn't take it
maybe how about this uh D6 is better than the coupon

claims.knob: D6 Tag value = savings on planned rerolls next shop (sum of normal costs - 0+1+2...); skip only if planned rerolls >= 3 and value beats round value

claims.statement: Double Tag is bad: it only pays if you take another skip later, and you shouldn't. Double + Orbital/Economy is great only on Anaglyph Deck, which stores Double Tags.

quotes.text: all right now double tag double tag sucks you know in theory in theory the double tag is as good as whatever the best tag that you would get is
that's not because the double tag is good that's because the anaglyph deck is good

claims.knob: Double Tag: never skip (except Anaglyph: value = best expected future tag)

claims.statement: 1.0.1: Rare/Uncommon/edition/Negative tags now make that shop joker free, and it still sells for its normal amount, so a joker that doesn't fit can be bought for $0 and sold for a few dollars. Skip in the same situations as before (round 1 Holographic/Foil), but this doesn't create new skip situations; most of the time you still don't skip. (White-stake framing.)

quotes.text: the rare tag now you're guaranteed uh in the next shop there's going to be a rare that rare is going to be free now
you can still pick it up for zero and then sell it for a couple bucks to make up for the loss
I think most of the time you still don't skip for them they're still problematic

claims.knob: tag joker price = 0 and fail-case value = sell value (~$1-3); keep skip allowlist unchanged (ante 1 Small: Holo/Foil/Uncommon/Coupon)
claims.notes: Current (1.0.1) view; supersedes the affordability point in q4YAHDuRUcQ.

claims.statement: At Orange/Gold stakes (1.0.1) a tag's joker can be Perishable (dies after 5 rounds), Rental ($3/round) or Eternal (can't sell, so free price doesn't help), which lowers joker tags; Top-up's jokers come unstickered.

quotes.text: if you take a Skip and you get a perishable polychrome or you get a perishable rare Joker
you could get Eternal Jokers where you can't sell them

claims.knob: at stakes with stickers: discount joker-tag value for P(perishable/rental/eternal); not relevant at White
claims.notes: Not relevant to the White-stake target.

claims.statement: Value Planets by +chips per level, because your +Mult comes from jokers and chips jokers are scarce. Straight (Saturn, +30 chips) is the best Planet in an 8-ante run: easy enough to assemble and high-scoring, so you play fewer hands. Start leveling Straights early.

quotes.text: The thing that matters most is the plus chips number because you get all of your plus mult from your jokers anyway
Straights are the sort of middle ground between being reasonable enough to assemble the hand, but then also being high enough scoring
I think then that means Saturn is the highest of all of the hands here

roffle.note: BU ranks Straight as the best planet/hand to level; Roffle says pick one cheap hand (High Card/Pair) when scoring comes from jokers.

claims.knob: planet value = chips_per_level weighted high, mult_per_level low; main-hand preference order starts with Straight; buy Saturn whenever straights are playable
claims.notes: Roffle's principle is conditional on joker/held-card scoring, so the conflict is partial.

claims.statement: In an 8-ante run Flush Five is out of reach unless you have Vagabond or Trading Card, and by then other hands are leveled; don't hold out for it. Flush House can be unlocked early with one suit-changing Tarot (pair + one card), so play it as early as you can; Ceres > Eris.

quotes.text: I think flush fives are out of reach unless you get very specific jokers like Vagabond or Trading Card
I'm going to play a flush house as early as I can
If you just keep holding, if you just keep waiting, it's just never going to happen

claims.knob: hand planner: never target Flush Five/Five of a Kind in antes 1-8 without deck-shaping jokers; allow Flush House as target once a suit-changer Tarot is available

claims.statement: His hand ordering for Planets (8-ante run): Four of a Kind > Five of a Kind (level 4oak from ante 1-2; 5oak needs unlock and is only ~15% more); Three of a Kind slightly > Full House (much easier, fine with low hand size); Flush > Three of a Kind (consistency); Two Pair (Uranus) is very reasonable, above Flush and Four of a Kind.

quotes.text: So, definitely four of a kind is above five of a kind
getting three of a kind is like way easier than getting full houses
I like it higher than flushes. I probably like it higher than four of a kind actually. I think I think two pair is a very reasonable hand to play

claims.knob: planet value table (relative): Saturn > Uranus > Jupiter > Venus > Earth; Mars > Planet X; Ceres > Eris; Mercury > Pluto
claims.notes: He wavers on Four of a Kind placement ('Maybe four of a kind goes down here').

claims.statement: Pluto is terrible and Mercury only slightly better. High Card builds win through jokers giving +Mult and +chips; with those jokers, hand levels don't matter.

quotes.text: Plutonium is terrible. It's just it's just not worth it.
if you have those jokers giving you plus 50 mult and plus 200 chips, then it doesn't matter what level your planets are

roffle.note: Roffle: pour every matching Planet into the cheap hand (High Card/Pair); BU: Pluto levels barely matter for High Card builds.

claims.knob: planet value Pluto ~ $0-1 (sell/skip), Mercury low; don't open Celestial packs for Pluto

claims.statement: When you play only one hand, Black Hole is equal to that hand's Planet, not better; Saturn edges it because The Fool can copy Saturn. Take Saturn over Black Hole even without a Fool in the shop. Use The Fool to copy your main Planet rather than for Hermit money.

quotes.text: if you're only ever playing just the one hand anyway, it's equal rather than strictly better in my opinion
do you take Saturn over black hole if there isn't a fool in the shop already? Yes, because there could be a fool in a future shop
if I have a fool, I would rather use the fool to copy the planet cards rather than giving me just the money

claims.knob: pack pick: main-hand Planet >= Black Hole when one main hand; Fool: use right after the main-hand Planet so it copies it

claims.statement: Leveling a hand has diminishing returns once you have many Planets, and with an xMult source (e.g. x2 Glass) you need fewer Planets than you'd think; early, deck manipulation (removal, Death copies) beats extra Planets.

quotes.text: once you have more planet cards, then you get like diminishing returns on leveling up your poker hands
if you have a source of X mult, if you have times two from the glass cards, I think you don't need as many planet cards as you might think

claims.knob: planet value multiplier decays with current hand level (e.g. x0.85 per level above 5, implied) and with owned xMult sources
claims.notes: The decay rate is not given; 'implied'.

claims.statement: Suit-changing Tarots (Star/Moon/Sun/World) are good enablers for flushes, flush house and straight flush: a higher hand needs fewer jokers, freeing slots for money. An early suit changer makes flushes easy (many flush jokers). Planets are still preferred for raw scoring. Rank them by the suit's payoff uncommon: Sun (Hearts/Bloodstone) > Moon (Clubs/Onyx Agate) > World (Spades/Arrowhead) > Star (Diamonds/Rough Gem, the money one, worst).

quotes.text: Suit changing tarot cards, pretty good. I think I'd rather have the planet cards for the increased scoring rather than the enabling
if you get a suit changer early on, then that makes it really easy to make flushes
we put uh Sun at the top here, hearts for bloodstone

claims.knob: suit changer target = the build's committed suit; value Sun > Moon > World > Star; take Planet over suit changer unless the build is flush-based and suit count is short

claims.statement: He would rather go all in on one suit than straddle suits; that is why Lovers (Wild cards) ranks low for him, and Wild cards are hit by all four suit-debuff bosses.

quotes.text: I'd rather just go all in on one suit rather than like kind of be on the the border here between different suits

claims.knob: Lovers value low; suit changers convert toward the single majority suit
claims.notes: Boss-debuff point raised by chat; he agrees.

claims.statement: The Hermit is worth about $20 once you're past the first couple of rounds (little in round 1). Its real value: a burst of money to clear out every pack in the shop without losing interest. Still, he takes Saturn (main-hand Planet) over Hermit every time, and Hanged Man over $20.

quotes.text: after you pass two rounds, then Hermit is 20 bucks
if you have the Hermit, then you can spend down. Like, you get this big burst of money and you can clear out the shop with that
